Definition: from G2784; a proclamation (especially of the gospel; by implication, the gospel itself):--preaching.
BiblicalUsage: Kerygma means a proclamation, the preaching itself: Matthew 12:41 says the men of Nineveh repented at the preaching of Jonas. 1 Corinthians 1:21 says it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe. 2 Timothy 4:17 says the Lord stood with Paul, that by me the preaching might be fully known, and all the Gentiles might hear. Titus 1:3 says God manifested his word through preaching, committed unto me.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the proclamation is the power: Nineveh repented at it, the Gentiles heard it, and God saves by its foolishness. I hold that preaching is not man's idea, it is God's chosen way to save, and I will not be ashamed of it.
